title: Design: New No Charge Category window shows its fields and helpers
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin (a user with every setting, See Financial Data included).
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 pixels wide at 100% zoom.
  • Have Internal Work Orders turned on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Use a location that is connected to QuickBooks Online, with every ShopView Accounts row mapped.
  • Start on Administration > Service > Internal Work Orders, No Charge categories tab.
  • Open the attached pictures iwo-flow0-06-2c-new-no-charge-category.png, iwo-happy-06-06-new-no-charge-category.png at 100% zoom beside the screen.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • A window titled "New No Charge Category" opens with a Name field.
  • Under "QuickBooks expense account" there is one account picker per connected location, each named after its location, with the helper "One per connected location, picked from the chart that is already in QuickBooks. Parts cost of this category posts here instead of Cost of Parts. Empty: posts to the ShopView Review account until you pick one."
  • An unticked checkbox "Requires the original work order" with the helper "The work order asks which earlier work order the job comes from, or Not in ShopView. Optional when the work order is created, required at Close."
  • Buttons Cancel and Save at the bottom right.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11758 (Story 1, Turn on Internal Work Orders, flag internal customers, manage categories)

  • S1-R14: “The category dialog ("New Internal Category", "New No Charge Category", or Edit with the current values) has: Name (required, unique within its list including archived categories, refused with "A category with this name is archived. Restore it instead."; 60 characters); "QuickBooks expense account", one picker per connected location listing that location's expense accounts (the same picker as the ShopView Accounts rows), with the helper "One per connected location, picked from the chart that is already in QuickBooks. Parts cost of this category posts here instead of Cost of Parts. Empty: posts to the ShopView Review account until you pick one."; on a No Charge category the checkbox "Requires the original work order" with the helper "The work order asks which earlier work order the job comes from, or Not in ShopView. Optional when the work order is created, required at Close."; on an Internal category the checkbox "Default category" with the helper "Used by internal customers that have no category of their own. One default at a time; it cannot be archived." Saving the account here and on the QuickBooks page (S5-R1) writes the same mapping; the account pickers are editable only with 'Settings — Integrations' and read-only with the text "Set in Integrations > QuickBooks" otherwise. The dialog shows the AccountingHub mapping as read-only text when the hub is enabled (the row is edited in the hub, S6-R1). A user without access to every connected location sees the pickers of the locations they can access; the other locations keep their mapping.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

References from Design

Design canvas "Internal Work Orders · All flows v6" (https://claude.ai/artifact/5jHR3nLeDinzks1viREFuo), version 1794484794-2031, read and rendered 12 Nov 2026: pages "Flow 0 · Turn it on" / "Happy flow v6", boards "2c New No Charge Category" (Flow 0 · Turn it on), "06 New No Charge category" (Happy flow v6).

Design pictures attached to this case:

  • iwo-flow0-06-2c-new-no-charge-category.png
  • iwo-happy-06-06-new-no-charge-category.png

The design's own words:

  • “Requires the original work order”
  • “One per connected location, picked from the chart that is already in QuickBooks.”

Difference: the design adds a helper under Name that says the category shows on the work order: register IWO-D09, question 12; the design's helper is its own held design-version case.
